cards.title: Oscilloscope in the web page with an on/off button
cards.description: A 440 Hz sine wave generated by the Rust engine (WASM in an AudioWorklet), played in the web page with an on/off button and shown live on an oscilloscope.

tasks.title: Install the Rust toolchain
engine-core: Object contract, strong types, fixed block, plan build and run (no_std, forbid unsafe)
engine-objects + engine-testkit: osc~ (440 Hz sine) passing the generic laws
engine-hash + engine-cli: offline render, canonical hash, first conformance case sine-440
bindings/wasm (engine-wasm + AudioWorklet glue): same hashes as native, proven by end-to-end tests on 4 browsers (OfflineAudioContext) and in Node
apps/playground: on/off button and live oscilloscope, end-to-end tests on 4 browsers
xtask check wired into CI and the pre-push hook
Independent conformance oracle (TypeScript): rereads the WAV of every case, recomputes the hashes and checks the expected signal, in cargo xtask check

cards.title: Patch format specification
cards.description: Versioned JSON Schema of a patch (boxes, cables, parameters): the contract shared by the engine, the SDKs, the editor, the AI assistant and MCP. Published with its reference documentation.

tasks.title: Version 1: boxes, parameters and cables (spec/patch-format.md, read by engine-patch)
JSON Schema of the format, published with its reference documentation
Box arguments (ports computed at creation, e.g. multichannel output) and the project's own box naming conventions

cards.title: HTML documentation site
cards.description: One site with guides, the API reference of every part (generated from docstrings), the box reference generated from the registry metadata and the patch format reference generated from the schema.

cards.title: Developer SDKs: Rust crate, npm package, C library
cards.description: Thin wrappers around the engine core for developers: a Rust crate, an npm package (WASM + TypeScript types, browser and Node) and a C library with a header (usable from C/C++, Swift, Kotlin, Python, Unity, Godot). Each one passes the same conformance corpus.

cards.title: Monorepo structure: spec, crates, bindings, apps, conformance
cards.description: Organize the repository as separate parts with clear contracts: the patch format spec, the reusable engine core, thin developer SDKs, the applications and the conformance corpus.

tasks.title: Document the parts and the monorepo layout in CLAUDE.md and README.md
Placeholder folders with a README each (spec, bindings, apps, conformance)
Move the roadmap to apps/roadmap
Root pnpm workspace (shared configs extracted later, when a second package needs them)
xtask, pre-push hook and CI updated for the new layout

cards.title: Choose and set up the project license
cards.description: Source-available, attribution required, commercial use allowed for artists, no competing product or service.

tasks.title: Choose the license (FSL-1.1-ALv2 or Elastic-2.0) and have it reviewed
Add LICENSE and set the SPDX identifier in Cargo.toml and every package.json
README: artists own what they create and may use it commercially
Contribution policy: DCO or CLA

cards.title: Choose the final project name
cards.description: The working name poyetik must be replaced before the first publication. Rename everywhere, then rewrite the git history in the same spirit so that no trace of the working name remains.

tasks.title: Find a name: short, easy to say in English and French, available (domain, GitHub, crates.io, npm) and free of trademark conflicts
Rename everywhere: folder, crates, packages, roadmap, docs, CI
Rewrite the git history so that no trace of the working name remains
Delete the local backup branch and purge the reflog before the first push

cards.title: Native bridge: OSC, MIDI, serial and HID over a local WebSocket
cards.description: A small open-source native companion (apps/bridge, Rust) that gives the web app what browsers cannot do (OSC over UDP, MIDI on Safari, serial, HID), over a local WebSocket. The app stays frontend-only and works without it. Released by CI for every platform.

tasks.title: Bridge: OSC, MIDI, serial and HID over a local WebSocket, with secure pairing (token and origin check)
Web app: detect the bridge and show which capabilities are available
CI build matrix and releases: binaries, checksums, provenance attestation, build-from-source instructions
Docs: how to run the unsigned binaries on macOS and Windows
Optional, later: code signing and notarization (macOS, Windows)

cards.title: Debug mode: JavaScript API to observe and drive the engine
cards.description: Enabled with ?debug in the web apps: one JavaScript API for people, AI agents driving a browser and the end-to-end tests, read-only on the audio side.

tasks.title: First version in the playground: help, snapshot, signal, levels, pitch, renderOffline
Readable text in the page for every measurement, plus debug.help()
Used by the playground end-to-end tests on 4 browsers
Documented, 100% coverage and mutation testing

cards.title: Reduce the size of the WebAssembly engine
cards.description: The proof of concept weighs 290 KB, largely the JSON reader (serde_json). Measure what each part costs, then shrink it (a lighter patch reader, wasm-opt, size-oriented build profile) without changing a single output sample: the conformance hashes must stay identical.
